ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Srinivasa Ramanujan — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Three months: abscess treatment complete, rifampin month two, blood count, liver tests, vitamins, mood, and plans to visit home

text.paragraph: Three months: abscess treatment complete, rifampin month two, blood count, liver tests, vitamins, mood, and plans to visit home. [S]

Mr. Ramanujan returns two weeks after his preventive visit. He has had no fever, pain, night sweats or diarrhea since the cold a month ago, and his weight is close to what it was before he fell ill. He is two months into rifampin, with no missed doses, nausea, rash or yellowing. He takes vitamin B12 and vitamin D daily. His hepatitis A antibody was positive, so he needs no vaccine for the trip, and the travel clinic has given him advice on malaria and food. He still sees the counselor, now every two weeks, calls home each Sunday, and has offered to teach a mathematics class at the Tamil association. He leaves for India in the summer and will take enough rifampin to finish the course there. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1917-04-20; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Warm and engaged; smiles when he talks about the class he will teach
Evening fevers to 38.6 °C with night sweats for about four weeks
S — Synthetic presenting symptom, superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Weight loss of 5 kg over two months (57 to 52 kg), with poor appetite
S — Synthetic presenting symptom, superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Dull right upper quadrant pain for three weeks, worse on deep breathing and lying on the right side, with a tender liver edge
S — Synthetic presenting symptom, superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Amebic liver abscess: a single 6.2 x 5.4 cm abscess in the right lobe (segment VII) on ultrasound, Entamoeba histolytica antibody positive, blood cultures negative, years after two episodes of dysentery in India; treated with metronidazole and then paromomycin; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to the hepatic amoebiasis later proposed for his illness
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; it does not settle the historical diagnostic conflict (CLM-0010, CLM-0011).
Vitamin B12 deficiency from a strict vegetarian diet (B12 168 pg/mL), with anemia (hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, MCV 99 fL) to which inflammation also contributes
S — Synthetic finding anchored to his documented diet and the vitamin deficiency later proposed.
S — Synthetic finding anchored to his documented diet and the vitamin deficiency later proposed.
Positive interferon-gamma release assay, with chest radiograph and sputum smears and NAAT negative for tuberculosis; cultures pending
S — Synthetic finding, superseded by the diagnosis of latent infection when cultures were negative.
Latent tuberculosis infection: positive interferon-gamma release assay, normal lungs on the radiograph, three sputum smears, NAAT and cultures negative; treated with four months of rifampin
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; active tuberculosis was excluded, which does not settle the historical question.
Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (PHQ-9 12, no thoughts of self-harm) during a serious illness, far from his wife and family
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented loneliness; not a claim about his real mental health.
Acute viral upper respiratory infection, three weeks into rifampin and six weeks after treatment of the liver abscess, without signs of abscess relapse; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Amebic liver abscess (A06.4). Resolved: no symptoms for three months, CRP 2 mg/L, alkaline phosphatase 96 U/L, weight regained. Any residual cavity on imaging could take months to disappear and does not need checking while he is well. [S]
No further imaging.
See a doctor promptly for fever or right-sided pain while traveling, and mention the abscess.

Latent tuberculosis infection (Z22.7). Two months of rifampin, adherent, without side effects; ALT 30, AST 26 U/L, bilirubin 0.7 mg/dL. [S]
Continue rifampin to complete four months.
A full supply for the trip, with a letter naming the medicine.
Completion check by video from India if needed.

Vitamin B12 deficiency with anemia (D51.3). Anemia resolved: hemoglobin 13.8 g/dL, MCV 90 fL; B12 520 pg/mL. [S]
Continue B12 daily, long term, on a vegetarian diet.

Vitamin D deficiency (E55.9). 25-hydroxyvitamin D 32 ng/mL after repletion, on 2,000 units daily with rifampin. [S]
Continue 2,000 units daily; recheck after rifampin ends.

Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.21). Remitting: PHQ-9 5 and GAD-7 4. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm; safety plan current; the 988 Lifeline cannot be reached from India, so the counselor gave him a crisis contact there for the trip. [S]
Counseling every two weeks until he travels; a video session while away if he wishes.

list.item: A diagnosis within days, with tuberculosis either confirmed or excluded before any treatment that could hide it. Outcome by 1917-02-23: Amebic liver abscess diagnosed at the second visit; active tuberculosis excluded by the radiograph, three smears, NAAT and cultures at six weeks [S]
No fever, the abscess treated, and the luminal course completed. Outcome by 1917-04-20: Afebrile by the third day of metronidazole; paromomycin completed; CRP and liver tests normal [S]
Regain at least half of the lost weight within three months, on a diet that keeps his rules. Outcome by 1917-04-20: 52.0 to 56.6 kg, nearly all the weight lost [S]
Vitamin B12 and vitamin D in the normal range and the anemia resolved. Outcome by 1917-04-20: B12 520 pg/mL; 25-hydroxyvitamin D 32 ng/mL; hemoglobin 13.8 g/dL [S]

PHQ-9 below 10 with no thoughts of self-harm, and regular contact with people who matter to him. Outcome by 1917-04-20: PHQ-9 12 to 5; weekly calls home and a weekly meal with others from his community [S]
Complete four months of rifampin for latent tuberculosis infection. Outcome by 1917-04-20: Month two of four; no side effects; liver tests normal [S]

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Guidelines for the Treatment of Latent Tuberculosis Infection: Recommendations from the National Tuberculosis Controllers Association and CDC, 2020 (2020); DPDx: Amebiasis (laboratory diagnosis, including antibody detection in extraintestinal disease) (2026); A Review of the Global Burden, New Diagnostics, and Current Therapeutics for Amebiasis (2018); Position of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics: Vegetarian Diets (2016); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, anemia and depression monographs (2026); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024)

Follow-up: Second hepatitis B dose before he travels. Completion of rifampin, by video from India if needed. Review on his return with vitamin D, a lipid panel and mood. Seek care promptly for fever or right-sided pain while away. [S]
